# The same-looking misstatement in the key spelling: `txn_guid:` +
# `txn_split_guid:` naming a 60.00 split while stating `amount: 999`.
#
# **Accepted**, where the directive form of it is refused — and that is the
# point of the fixture. `amount:` does not mean the same figure on the two
# spellings. On a block naming its splits it is what they come to. On this one
# `_bank_side_figure_of` reads it as what moved through the bank, residue and
# all, which is what the overpayment remedy prints: `amount: 120` beside a
# 100.00 split and `prepayment: 20`. Weighing it against the split the key
# gives refuses the remedy this tool itself prints.
#
# So the two are asked different questions deliberately, and README says which
# is which.
#
# What this fixture produces: a clean import, with that split settling
# the invoice by its own 60.00.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 999
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    txn_guid: "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
    txn_split_guid: "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
